To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
meander bends in a lowland river display coherent patterns of velocity, bed topographic features, lower-regime dunes, and bed-material texture.
meander bends in a large sand-bed river display coherent patterns of cross-sectional maxima for current velocity, bed depth, mean size, and height of bed forms.

meander bends in a lowland river of Illinois and Indiana are characterized by coherent patterns of current-velocity magnitude, bed topography (depth), lower-regime bed-form size, and bed-material grain size.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the velocity–bed-form– texture patterns of the lower Wabsh River meander bends are the result of the combined effects of the following three processes: (1) spiral flow, (2) bed topography, and (3) the interaction between flow and bed topography.

the lower Wabass River displays a sequence of coherent patterns of velocity, topography, and bed material in meander bends, and that the sequence of patterns of increasing transition length is: spiral flow, velocity magnitude, topography, bed material, and bed forms.
the velocity–bed form–texture patterns of a meander bend in the lower Wubash River are controlled by the flow regime and the sediment regime of the stream.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the velocity–bed-form–bed-material-size patterns of meander bend zones in a given river reach are a function of the stream discharge.

the transitional zone for velocity-magnitude patterns in meander bends of the lower Wabass River is a zone of maximum dune and sand-wave development and that the transitional zone of maximum dunes and sand-wave development in meander bends is a zone of greatest velocity-magnitude change.
a given bend is characterized by a velocity–bed-form–size pattern that is a composite of the patterns of the preceding and following meander bends.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bed-form–flow–sediment patterns in meander bends are coherent.
the velocity–bed-form–bed-texture patterns of meander bend zones are coherent and predictable.
the spatial pattern of bed forms and bed texture in a meander bend is a function of the spatial pattern of velocity magnitude and direction in the bend.
